checks.invariant: A member cannot create a time_entries row in a reviewed (approved) state without an admin transition
checks.result: enforce_status_rules is attached only as BEFORE UPDATE (schema.sql:86-88, setup.sql:100-103); the INSERT policy checks only user_id = auth.uid() (schema.sql:53-54, setup.sql:72-73). No INSERT trigger, CHECK constraint or column restriction on status exists in any SQL file, so a member-supplied status='approved' on INSERT is not rejected by any source-visible control. The client itself sends status explicitly (entries.ts:41). Candidate raised; column grants and applied-SQL are deployment facts.

checks.invariant: Once an entry is approved, its member owner cannot change the reviewed quantities (duration_seconds, started_at, ended_at)
checks.result: The member UPDATE policy has no column restriction (schema.sql:58-60, setup.sql:76-77) and the trigger compares only status (schema.sql:78, setup.sql:93). The client already writes duration_seconds computed in the browser (entries.ts:53-56). A member can therefore rewrite duration/timestamps on an approved row while status stays 'approved'. Candidate raised.

checks.invariant: Award/leaderboard derives only from admin-reviewed, bounded durations
checks.result: computeMonthlyAward and monthlyLeaderboard sum stored duration_seconds of rows with status 'approved' and endedAt, bucketed by started_at month (awards.ts:18-23,54-58); normalizeSeconds only clamps negatives/NaN (time.ts:6-9), so any positive integer up to the Postgres integer max (2147483647) counts. The admin console computes the award from listAllEntries (admIn/page.tsx:32,74-75). The derived award trusts row data written by the member paths above.

checks.invariant: Status transitions by members (pending->approved, rejected->approved) are blocked on UPDATE
checks.result: Held: the BEFORE UPDATE trigger raises when not is_admin() and new.status is distinct from old.status (schema.sql:78-80). reviewEntry (entries.ts:85) relies on this plus the admin UPDATE policy (schema.sql:64-65).

checks.invariant: Members cannot read, update or delete other members' time_entries rows
checks.result: Held: SELECT using (user_id = auth.uid() or is_admin()) (schema.sql:48-49); member UPDATE using and with check user_id = auth.uid() (schema.sql:58-60) prevents both targeting and reassigning another user's row; DELETE admin-only (schema.sql:69-70); RLS enabled (schema.sql:44). setup.sql:65-85 is identical. listMyEntries' .eq('user_id') filter (entries.ts:69) is not relied upon; listAllEntries (entries.ts:78) relies on RLS, which returns only own rows to members.

checks.invariant: RLS write policies bind the review-controlled columns (status, duration) for member writes
checks.result: Not held: INSERT with check and member UPDATE with check constrain only user_id (schema.sql:54,60); status/duration/timestamps are unconstrained on INSERT and duration/timestamps on UPDATE. Same root causes as the business-logic unit candidates.

checks.invariant: Alternate read path (Realtime publication) does not widen access
checks.result: setup.sql:110-127 adds time_entries to supabase_realtime with replica identity full, but no client code subscribes (no channel/postgres_changes in src/). Realtime enforces RLS for authenticated postgres_changes by provider design; not decisive for this unit, recorded as hardening.

checks.invariant: admin_create_user refuses non-admin callers before any write
checks.result: Held: first statement is `if not public.is_admin() then raise` (admin-create-user.sql:38-40); variable initializers (33-36) perform no writes. EXECUTE revoked from public/anon and granted to authenticated (98-99). is_admin() reads auth.jwt()->app_metadata->>role (schema.sql:37-40), which PostgREST populates only after verifying the JWT signature; app_metadata is not user-writable via GoTrue updateUser.

checks.invariant: Caller-supplied role/confirmation fields cannot escape intended values
checks.result: Held: p_role coerced to 'admin' or 'member' (admin-create-user.sql:34); only an already-verified admin reaches the insert, and admin creating admins is intended. Email regex/length/disposable checks and duplicate check run server-side (43-65); password is bcrypt-hashed (77). src/lib/auth.ts:80-86 passes values straight through, which is fine because the server enforces.

checks.invariant: admin_list_users discloses auth.users only to admins
checks.result: Held: is_admin() check before the query (admin-create-user.sql:119-121); revoke from public/anon, grant authenticated (135-136). Returned columns are limited to id, email, display_name, role, confirmation flag, created_at (124-129); no password hashes or tokens.

checks.invariant: SECURITY DEFINER functions cannot be hijacked through search_path by lower-trust callers
checks.result: search_path is pinned (admin-create-user.sql:30,116) but lists public before extensions, so unqualified crypt/gen_salt/gen_random_uuid (36,77,89) would resolve to a public-schema shadow if one existed. Creating such a function requires DDL, which members cannot issue via PostgREST; no member path to plant it. Recorded as hardening, not a finding.

checks.invariant: Only a GoTrue-verified admin can reach the service-role invite
checks.result: Held: the bearer token is verified server-side by caller.auth.getUser() against GoTrue (index.ts:24-30), and role comes from the returned user record's app_metadata (31-34), not from an unverified decode. A missing or garbage Authorization header yields userErr -> 401. The service-role client is created only after both checks (47).

checks.invariant: Request body cannot set privileged attributes on the invited user
checks.result: Held: body.role is parsed but never used (36, 48-50); only display_name goes into user metadata, so invitees get no app_metadata role (member by default). Nothing in src/ calls this function.

candidates.title: Members can insert pre-approved time entries with arbitrary duration, skipping admin review and inflating the monthly award
candidates.description: The status guard enforce_status_rules runs only BEFORE UPDATE. The INSERT RLS policy checks only user_id = auth.uid(). Any authenticated member holding the public anon key and their own session can POST to PostgREST /rest/v1/time_entries with {user_id: self, status: 'approved', started_at: <this month>, ended_at: <any>, duration_seconds: 2147483647}. The row is then counted by computeMonthlyAward/monthlyLeaderboard in the admin console, and the member is shown as the monthly Top Timer, without any admin ever approving it. The admin review queue shows the row as already approved.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The review-state invariant (only admins set status to approved/rejected) is enforced only on UPDATE (trigger trg_status_guard BEFORE UPDATE), while the INSERT path (RLS 'insert own' with check user_id = auth.uid()) accepts client-supplied status and quantity columns with no trigger, CHECK constraint, or column privilege restricting them.

trace.description: Client inserts into time_entries with a client-chosen status field; any member can send the same PostgREST insert with status 'approved' and arbitrary duration/timestamps.
INSERT with check constrains only user_id = auth.uid(); status, duration_seconds, started_at, ended_at are unchecked (identical in supabase/setup.sql:73).
Status guard is declared 'before update' only, so it never fires on INSERT (identical in supabase/setup.sql:102).
Admin console computes the award and leaderboard from all rows returned by listAllEntries.
Sums duration_seconds of rows with status 'approved', so the self-approved, inflated row wins the monthly award.

evidence.description: for insert with check (user_id = auth.uid()) - no status or duration constraint.
before update on public.time_entries - trigger does not cover INSERT.
status column has a default but no CHECK restricting inserts to 'pending'; duration_seconds (line 20) has no bound.
Award counts any row whose status is 'approved' and has an endedAt; no provenance of the approval is checked.
normalizeSeconds only clamps negative/NaN values; large positive durations pass.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox on this host, so a local Postgres/PostgREST dummy-member insert could not be executed.
Table/column privileges for role authenticated on public.time_entries are not in source (Supabase default privileges normally grant INSERT on all columns, but the deployed grants are not observable).
Which SQL file(s) (schema.sql vs setup.sql) were applied to the deployed project, and whether any later out-of-repo migration added an INSERT trigger or CHECK, is not source-visible.

validation_plan.local: In a sandboxed local Supabase/Postgres with the auth schema, apply supabase/setup.sql, create two dummy users (member M, admin A), set request.jwt.claims to M's claims (role authenticated, sub=M, app_metadata.role=member) and run: insert into public.time_entries(user_id,status,started_at,ended_at,duration_seconds) values ('<M>','approved',now(),now(),2147483647) returning status; expected vulnerable result is a row with status 'approved'. Then feed the rows to computeMonthlyAward with a unit test and observe M as winner.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner, in the Supabase SQL editor: select tgname, tgtype from pg_trigger where tgrelid='public.time_entries'::regclass; and select privilege_type, column_name from information_schema.column_privileges where table_name='time_entries' and grantee='authenticated'. If INSERT on status is granted and no insert trigger exists, the path is open; optionally confirm with a dummy member account in a staging project.

candidates.title: Members can rewrite duration and timestamps of already-approved entries, inflating award totals after review
candidates.description: The member UPDATE policy allows the owner to update any column of their own rows, and enforce_status_rules only rejects status changes. After an admin approves an entry, the owning member can PATCH /rest/v1/time_entries?id=eq.<id> with {duration_seconds: 2147483647} or move started_at into the current month. The status stays 'approved', the trigger passes, and the award/leaderboard in the admin console counts the new value. The client code itself sends a browser-computed duration_seconds (stopEntry), so the server never derives or freezes the reviewed quantity.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Approval is recorded on status only; the reviewed quantities (duration_seconds, started_at, ended_at) remain owner-writable via the 'update own not status' policy (no column restriction) and the trigger compares only new.status vs old.status, so approval does not freeze what was approved.

trace.description: Member client sends update({ ended_at, duration_seconds }) with a browser-computed duration; any member can send arbitrary values for any own row, including approved ones.
using/with check user_id = auth.uid() only - no column or status-state restriction (identical in supabase/setup.sql:77).
Trigger raises only when status changes; duration/timestamp edits on approved rows pass.
Leaderboard and award (awards.ts:23) sum the mutated duration_seconds of approved rows.

evidence.description: with check (user_id = auth.uid()) - no restriction on duration_seconds/started_at/ended_at.
if not public.is_admin() and new.status is distinct from old.status - only status is guarded.
Duration is computed client-side and trusted by the server.
Admin console leaderboard derived from the stored duration values.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox on this host, so a local Postgres dummy-member update could not be executed.
Deployed column UPDATE privileges for role authenticated on public.time_entries and any out-of-repo triggers are not source-visible.

validation_plan.local: In a sandboxed local Postgres with setup.sql applied: as admin claims, insert a row for dummy member M and set status='approved'; switch request.jwt.claims to M and run update public.time_entries set duration_seconds=2147483647 where id='<row>' returning status, duration_seconds; the vulnerable result is status 'approved' with the new duration and no exception.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks pg_trigger on public.time_entries for any trigger freezing columns on approved rows and information_schema.column_privileges for authenticated UPDATE on duration_seconds/started_at/ended_at; optionally repeat the update with a dummy member in a staging project.

hardening: supabase/admin-create-user.sql:30 and :116 set search_path with public before extensions/auth and call crypt/gen_salt/gen_random_uuid unqualified (lines 36,77,89); qualify as extensions.crypt/extensions.gen_salt and use search_path = '' or pg_catalog, pg_temp-last to remove the shadowing class.

supabase/schema.sql:37-40 is_admin() trusts the JWT app_metadata.role claim, so an admin demoted in auth.users keeps admin RLS/RPC rights until the access token expires; keep JWT expiry short or check auth.users in is_admin() if immediate revocation matters.

supabase/schema.sql:18-21 has no CHECK constraints (duration_seconds >= 0 and bounded, ended_at >= started_at); add them with a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that forces status='pending' for non-admin inserts, freezes approved rows for members, and derives duration_seconds server-side from ended_at - started_at.

supabase/functions/admin-create-user/index.ts:52 returns raw GoTrue error.message to the (admin) caller, and index.ts:9 imports an unpinned esm.sh URL; neither is reachable by a lower-trust principal and the function is not called from src/.

supabase/setup.sql:110-127 publishes time_entries to supabase_realtime with replica identity full although no client subscribes; drop it from the publication if unused, which shrinks the read surface to PostgREST alone.

supabase/admin-create-user.sql:145-149 runs unconditional lowercasing UPDATEs on auth.users/auth.identities every time the file is run; if two accounts differ only by case, this can collide or merge identities. Run it once, deliberately, after a duplicate check.

uncovered.boundary: admin_list_users display_name rendering in admin console review queue / leaderboard / award (supabase/admin-create-user.sql:126, src/app/time/Portal/admIn/page.tsx:61,66)
uncovered.reason: display_name is read from user-writable raw_user_meta_data and is the primary label the admin uses to identify whose entries they approve and who won the award; a member can rename themselves to another member's name or to an admin-looking label. That identity-display integrity issue (not XSS, which a peer owns) has no current coverage unit.
